+== Security and HTML Escaping
 
-Examples include observability, security, configuration, and error handling.
+Stem does not perform automatic HTML escaping; `{{ expression }}` renders the expression result directly as a string.
+Any output transformation, including sanitization and escaping, must be done explicitly through helper functions (e.g., `{{name |> escape_html}}`) or ordinary Elixir function calls used in expressions.
+
+Keeping the rendering model to one expression form removes ambiguous output modes and makes security-sensitive formatting decisions explicit at the call site.
+Callers must treat all dynamically selected templates and user-provided context as untrusted, applying sanitization at the output boundary.
+
+== Explicit Data Boundaries
+
+Stem preserves an explicit boundary between data and templates at all levels.
+In the CLI, the command contract differentiates between file-backed JSON (`mix stem data.json template.stem`) and stdin-piped JSON (`echo '{}' | mix stem template.stem`), avoiding implicit ambiguity parsing strings versus files.
+
+== Whitespace Control
+
+Stem provides declarative, tag-level whitespace control using the `~` character.
+Whitespace logic allows adjusting spacing around rendered content without littering source files with unreadable formatting:
+
+* `{{~ ... ~}}`: Trims literal whitespace symmetrically before and after the tag.
+* `{{~ ... }}` and `{{ ... ~}}`: Trims whitespace precisely on the given side (one-sided trim).

+=== ADR-0003: Explicit Data Boundaries and CLI Contract
+
+Accepted (2026-05-21).
+
+*Context.* The CLI previously allowed flexible inline JSON data directly in the positional arguments (`stem template.stem '{"key": "value"}'`), which mixed string evaluation with file paths.
+
+*Decision.* Remove inline JSON from the positional CLI contract. Establish a Mustache-style contract: one argument (`stem template.stem`) means the template gets bound to JSON read from standard input. Two arguments (`stem data.json template.stem`) mean file-backed data first, then the template.
+
+*Consequences.* The CLI behavior is strictly file-based or pipe-based, avoiding ambiguity and reinforcing Stem's philosophy of explicit data separation and strict input boundaries.

-* local development workflow
-* build and test commands
-* release or deployment procedure
-* troubleshooting and recovery steps
+Stem ships with an explicit, file-centric CLI that allows you to easily format and execute templates from your shell.
+
+=== Formatting Templates
+
+To format your `.stem` template files, use the `mix stem.format` task:
+
+[source,sh]
+----
+mix stem.format "lib/**/*.stem"
+mix stem.format --check-formatted path/to/template.stem
+----
+
+=== Rendering Templates
+
+The CLI supports strict file or standard input models for binding data, modeled after standard Mustache CLI tooling conventions.
+
+*File-backed Data and Template:*
+When providing two positional arguments, the first specifies a JSON data file and the second points to the `.stem` template file:
+
+[source,sh]
+----
+mix stem data.json template.stem
+----
+
+*Standard Input Interpolation:*
+When providing a single positional argument, the CLI reads the JSON object from the pipeline standard input and applies it to the template:
+
+[source,sh]
+----
+echo '{"name":"Nina"}' | mix stem template.stem
+----
+
+By isolating the data into standalone files or pipes, there is no ambiguity parsing raw strings vs files on the command line.

 == What This Project Is

+Stem is a native template compiler for Elixir that fuses the familiar syntax of Handlebars with the attribute strictness of StringTemplate and the powerful transformation pipelines of Jinja2. It compiles double-curly-brace (`{{ }}`) templates directly into Elixir's abstract syntax tree.
+
+Unlike earlier templating efforts that translated text via EEx, Stem owns the entire pipeline from lexing to macro generation, offering exact compile-time checks, fast rendering performance, and explicit security models.
